Your records live in a local database on this device and are never uploaded. The one network request the app can make is the update check: a read-only request to the configured releases address, carrying no ledger data and no identifier. Export and import work on a local JSON file you choose.
The full licence text of each component is available at its project page.

A damaged or older database can no longer lock you out, the entry form keeps what you typed through a rotation or theme change, the first frame stops showing a balance of zero, dark mode no longer opens with a white flash, and an oversized import can no longer exhaust the memory available.

First beta: preference reads and writes can no longer take the app down, a failed delete says so instead of crashing, an export is taken in one piece, and the hot queries were checked against the database indexes.

A quick flick no longer deletes without a buzz, the statistics date stops moving when the jump-to-today line appears, and the language list is ordered by language code instead of starting with Chinese.
Fixes the swipe-to-delete that stopped working, keeps the buzz when a swipe has gone far enough, and removes the rightward swipe on a row — it could not feel the same as swiping the page.

The balance is green in surplus and red in debt, a delete swipe now has to be deliberate and buzzes when it is, swiping a row right turns to Statistics, and the statistics date offers a way back to today.
Fixes the category buttons that could disappear from the entry form, and the currency picker now offers nine signs on their own with no currency names beside them.

Daily use fixes: the newest entry is no longer hidden behind the add button, the keyboard no longer covers the save action, the form works again when every category has been deleted, dates and clock times follow your language, counted text uses proper plural forms, and a damaged settings file no longer stops the app from starting.

The statistics breakdown now splits each category by the direction its transactions were recorded with, so re-typing a category no longer moves money to the other side of the screen or makes the donut disagree with the totals above it.

Amounts typed on a comma keyboard are read correctly instead of being multiplied by a hundred, a backup carrying no records is refused rather than erasing the ledger, and the update dialog shows release notes as text instead of Markdown.

The update check falls back to the GitHub release feed when the API refuses or cannot be read, says which failure happened instead of one sentence for all of them, and waits longer on a slow connection.
First published build: manual entry with categories and notes, a day-grouped month view, year/month/day statistics, nine languages and JSON backup.
